_note: VOX-026. The scripted demo session: ten turns, one barge-in, two confirmations. Driven by
scripts/dry_run.py, which runs it end to end with no microphone and asserts every `expect`.
This is NOT an eval split. It is a rehearsal script — the running order of a demo, written
down so the same session can be run twice and compared. Four of the questions are copies of
evals/dev/pdf_queries.json (q05, q04, q02, q06, q09, q10 by their ids there), which means
nothing here bounds how much the system was tuned to them: they were chosen *because* they
are known-good, which is what a demo wants and what an eval must never be. Any number this
file produces is a dev number and the report says so.
evals/heldout/ is untouched by this file. Nothing here is drawn from it, and a rehearsal is
not a gate — it prints latencies and a pass/fail per turn, not a score.
`say` is the user's line. It is synthesised locally (see scripts/dry_run.py --user-voice) into
a cached wav and handed to the real STT stage, so the run needs no person and no mic. Put a
path in `recording` instead and that file is used verbatim — which is how a real recorded
voice replaces a synthetic one for the demo-machine rehearsal.
Ordering is deliberate. t02-t03 are the two clean grounded answers you open with. t04 is the
long one, so there is something to interrupt, and its interruption becomes t05's input the way
the live loop carries it. t06 and t07 are the two different refusals — floor-rejected and
model-refused — because a demo that only shows answers has not shown the interesting half.
t08 confirms and proceeds, t09 confirms and cancels. t10 ends on the escalation path, which is
the honest note to end an internal assistant demo on.

turns.why: Opens the session and proves the chain end to end before anything harder. No document covers a greeting, so it is the plain reply path by construction.

turns.say: how many maternity leaves does a woman employee get
turns.why: pdf_queries q05 — the control. A clean single-page answer in the largest document; if this one is not grounded, the index is wrong and the demo stops here.

turns.say: what are the standard office working hours and shift timings
turns.why: pdf_queries q04. The answer is nothing but figures, so it is the turn that exercises answer.ungrounded_numbers() on a reply that must be allowed to state numbers.

turns.say: what happens to my laptop if I resign before two years of allotment

barge_with.say: actually, what is the dress code in the office

turns.why: pdf_queries q07: a conditional answer rather than a lookup, so it is long enough to be worth interrupting. after_s is when the user starts talking over the reply; it has to be shorter than the reply and longer than the output buffer, or abort() cuts nothing and the barge-in is a silent non-event.
turns.not_q02: This turn was written as q02 (privilege leave encashment) and the first dry run cut it. Whisper returned 'How is my privilege leaving CashMint calculated when I leave the company?' from a clean synthetic voice — the same damage ARCHITECTURE.md records from a live turn, where 'leave encashment' came back as 'leaving cashment'. Retrieval then returned leave-policy p9/p11 instead of separation-policy p13/p26, and the turn answered fluently from the wrong document. It is q03 in pdf_queries.json for exactly this reason, and it is not a question to ask in front of an audience while VOX_STT_BIAS is off.

turns.why: No `say` of its own: this turn runs on the audio that interrupted t04, exactly as the live loop's `pending` does. That is the half of VOX-011 a recording usually cannot show.
turns.label_note: p12, not the p13 that evals/dev/pdf_queries.json labels for the same question. The dress code itself is on p12 — chunk 16 is 'The same dress code applies to remote working in office' and chunk 17 is the men's and women's wear lists — while p13 carries only the note about what happens to someone who violates it. That was read off runs/chunks.jsonl before this label was written, which is the rule pdf_queries.json states for its own labels. The disagreement is reported to the Evaluator rather than fixed here: q06's label is scored by VOX-033's gate and changing it changes a gate number, which is not this ticket's to change.

turns.say: what is the health insurance coverage amount for my family
turns.why: pdf_queries q10, the floor-rejected absent query: nothing clears RETRIEVAL_SCORE_FLOOR, so the turn takes the plain path and the extractor answers it. `intent_in` is the assertion that matters — a corpus miss must come back as not-knowing, not as a confident invention.

turns.say: how many days of paid menstrual leave does the company give
turns.why: pdf_queries q09, the other refusal and the expensive one: it clears the floor on leave-policy chunks about other leave types, so the model has to refuse from excerpts that look relevant. `grounded` false with `retrieved` non-zero is exactly that event on the record.

turns.say: book a one hour meeting with Priya tomorrow at three p.m.
turns.why: VOX-020. A request, not a question — retrieval does not claim it, so the extractor runs and asks for confirmation with the details read back. Nothing is written by a yes: the ticket's constraint is no real account changes, and the confirmed branch is a print.

turns.say: log four hours on the VOX project for today
turns.why: The same gate answered the other way, because a confirmation you can only say yes to is not a gate. The cancel reply is spoken, so this turn has a second TTS call — timed as t_confirm_tts_ms and not over the top of the read-back's t_tts_ms.

turns.say: I need to escalate this to the engineering lead
turns.why: Ends on the path that hands a person to a person. An internal assistant that cannot say 'this is not mine to answer' is the one nobody trusts, and it is a one-line demo of the escalate intent that costs no corpus and no confirmation.
